question.text:
Which of the following is the correct negation of the statement "There exists a living person who is 150 years old"?

  1. There exists a living person who is not 150 years old.
  2. No living person is exactly 150 years old.
  3. There exists a living person who is at most 149 years old.
  4. Every living person is 150 years old.
question.subject: Mathematical Logic

question.text:
Which of the following is the correct negation of the statement "For all positive integers n, $\mathrm{n}+2>8^{\prime \prime}$ ?

  1. For all positive integers $n, n+2 \leqslant 8$.
  2. There exists a positive integer n such that $\mathrm{n}+2>8$.
  3. There exists a positive integer n such that $\mathrm{n}+2 \leqslant 8$.
  4. For no positive integer n do we have $\mathrm{n}+2>8$.
question.subject: Mathematical Logic

question.text:
Let $\mathrm{p}=$ "It is below freezing" and $\mathrm{q}=$ "It is snowing." Which of the following correctly translates: "That it is below freezing is necessary and sufficient for it to be snowing"?

  1. $\mathrm{p} \rightarrow \mathrm{q}$
  2. $\mathrm{q} \rightarrow \mathrm{p}$
  3. $p \leftrightarrow q$
  4. $\mathrm{p} \wedge \mathrm{q}$
question.subject: Mathematical Logic

question.text:
A formula of the form $\mathrm{P} ightarrow \mathrm{Q}$ is said to be valid (a tautology) when its antecedent P is always FALSE - this is called a vacuous truth. In the formula $ eg( eg \mathrm{A} ightarrow \mathrm{B}) \wedge \mathrm{A} \wedge \mathrm{C} ightarrow \mathrm{Q}$, the antecedent $ eg( eg \mathrm{A} ightarrow \mathrm{B}) \wedge \mathrm{A} \wedge \mathrm{C}$ is always FALSE because:

  1. $ eg( eg \mathrm{A} ightarrow \mathrm{B}) \wedge \mathrm{A}$ is itself a contradiction for all values of A and B .
  2. C is always FALSE.
  3. The consequent Q is always TRUE.
  4. $ eg( eg \mathrm{A} ightarrow \mathrm{B}) \wedge \mathrm{A} \wedge \mathrm{C}$ requires $\mathrm{A} \wedge eg \mathrm{A}$ to hold simultaneously.
question.subject: Mathematical Logic

question.text:
Let p = "It is below freezing" and q = "It is snowing." Which of the following correctly translates: "Either it is below freezing or it is snowing, but it is not snowing if it is below freezing"?

  1. $(\mathrm{p} \vee \mathrm{q}) \wedge(\mathrm{q} ightarrow eg \mathrm{p})$
  2. $(\mathrm{p} \vee \mathrm{q}) \wedge eg(\mathrm{p} \wedge \mathrm{q})$
  3. $(\mathrm{p} \vee \mathrm{q}) \wedge(\mathrm{p} ightarrow eg \mathrm{q})$
  4. $(\mathrm{p} \oplus \mathrm{q}) \wedge(\mathrm{p} ightarrow \mathrm{q})$
question.subject: Mathematical Logic
